I really like it.

The game opens up with a world where superheroes are already established and how a corporation could handle them, but the characters are the main focus, with Invisigal and Blonde Blazer being the highlights that really make you invested in their journeys (especially when you're romancing them). And even if romance isn't your style, it doesn't take away from the fact that both of them are very likeable and easy to root for, along with the other characters.

The gameplay is pretty intuitive and easy to pick up (if you pay attention), and the fact that the choices you make impact the characters' attitudes in a way that directly affects you during Dispatching just helps make the world feel real and lived-in, especially with the banter and jokes they throw around during it.

Getting both the romantic endings with either Invisigal or Blonde Blazer isn't very demanding, and it helps that the dialogue is diverse enough that you can change how a lot of scenes play out in a replay so it feels like a different experience with each one.

But I will say that not being able to skip/speed up the cutscenes and dialogue really hurts the replay value, because outside of romancing both of them I don't really like the idea of playing another few hours of this game for another ending just because of how much time I will lose seeing repeated cutscenes.

Overall, a very good game with a great story and engaging gameplay. Solid 8/10.

Engaging story, great imagery, and top-notch voice acting.  I found the primary game-play loop of dispatching heroes to resolve issues a bit frustrating because the description of what's needed is very vague in matching up against what hero's abilities best fit that mission (some were obvious; fighting a Kaiju needs combat & vigor, defusing a bomb needs intellect, but many missions were unclear to me about what hero was needed).  Also some missions are just flat-out failures (the game tells you this) and that just sucks in a game design.  I also found some of the animated cut-scenes with interspersed combat decisions (click on a tight timer or slide the click-slide the mouse with a release on a tight timer) to be a bit off-putting as I had no training on this before it happened and was caught off-guard more than once just being immersed in a cut-scene that turned out to be combat requiring real-time precision input actions.  Despite those issues I had, lots of more twitch-intuitive gamers probably would like this style and the story, imagery, and narration far outweighed the mechanical disappointments for me personally.  Would definitely recommend as it's still a great value for the purchase cost, but probably not at the top of my suggestion list.

Dispatch Review: The Ultimate Interactive Superhero Series

Dispatch is nothing short of an exceptional gaming experience. From the very first minute, it wraps you in an immersive, highly cinematic atmosphere that makes you feel as though you aren't just playing a game, but actively watching and starring in a high-stakes animated series like Invincible—except this time, you hold the script. Every choice you make shapes the narrative, steering the story and the fate of its characters in profound ways.

What makes Dispatch an absolute triumph is how masterfully it balances its storytelling. It truly has a bit of everything:

Razor-sharp humor that hits at just the right moments,

Genuinely moving romance and human connection,

Heartbreaking betrayal that keeps you on the edge of your seat,

Powerful arcs of redemption and revenge that make every decision feel heavy and meaningful.

It is a flawless recipe for a smash hit. The blending of tactical dispatcher mechanics with deeply branchable, character-driven storytelling sets a new gold standard for interactive narrative games.

I sincerely hope the studio continues down this path and releases more titles like this in the future—Dispatch is a masterpiece that demands to be played!

[h1]One of the best games I've played in a while.[/h1]

Unlike many, I had never spent much time playing the Telltale-era games that were so based on choice (the most experience I ever got was the Batman game and Minecraft Story Mode, and those were great). This game was a combination of that same pressure you feel when a big decision needs to be made, but it's blended with incredible animation, addicting (and yet very straightforward) gameplay, and top-tier voice acting. All those things together make the story one I cared a lot about, and will probably keep anyone's attention.

I can say that this was one of the most fun times I've had playing a single-player game in a while, and I'm convinced that that title won't budge anytime soon (maybe except for a season two, fingers crossed). I even plan on coming back for a second playthrough, its just that good.

Back in the day, I was a huge fan of Telltale Games, and this one reminded me so much of those times. It’s an almost classic superhero story about not-so-heroic ex-villains where you decide who they might become in the end.

I loved all the characters, even those with less than 5 minutes of screen time (Sonar, my goat...). All the Z-team members change and go through their own redemption arcs — or don't, depending on the choices you make. Some characters even managed to surprise me in later episodes. I’ll definitely try recruiting Waterboy to my team in the next playthrough.

Storywise, the game is okay. A few things felt awkward or rushed, especially the romance subplots. The villains changed their attitude and behavior in just a few months: starting out as huge hypocritical egoists and turning into people who actually care about each other as a team, which felt a bit strange. Major decisions do make you face consequences, but some of them feel too severe.

[spoiler] In my first and only playthrough so far, Invisigal went back to being a villain. I suppose it's because I fired her? Kinda stupid, since from the first episode to the last I did nothing but support her, encouraging her that she is the sole maker of her fate... In that sense, Coupe or Sonar being sour about being kicked out at the start of the Phoenix program makes much more sense. [/spoiler]

The gameplay is a lot of fun! Some things Robert can do himself by hacking, but most of the time you’re thinking about sending out the best hero for the job. Listening to the banter is my favorite part — it really makes up for the lack of screen time for the background characters. In later episodes, there’s less gameplay and more story, so you won't get tired of repetitive management.

Overall, a very solid game for a couple of evenings that keeps you fully engaged.

**9.5/10 – Un véritable coup de cœur!**

WOW! Je viens de terminer Dispatch en deux jours. DEUX JOURS! Je ne me souviens même pas de la dernière fois où j'ai dévoré un jeu aussi rapidement. Je voulais constamment savoir ce qui allait arriver ensuite!

**L'histoire : 10/10.** Absolument excellente! Les personnages sont attachants, les dialogues sont savoureux et les choix ont suffisamment de poids pour nous faire réfléchir. Évidemment, les décisions proposées ne correspondent pas toujours à ce que MOI j'aurais fait, mais bon, c'est pas moi qui écris l'histoire! 😂

**Les graphismes, les animations, la musique, les sons et l'ambiance : 10/10.** Tout fonctionne merveilleusement bien ensemble. Et les acteurs? WOW! Les performances sont absolument remarquables.

Mon seul véritable reproche concerne la gestion du dispatch. Je trouve que les mécaniques sont vraiment mal expliquées. J'ai terminé le jeu et je ne suis toujours pas certain de comprendre comment bien choisir mes héros pour les différentes missions. J'étais franchement pourri! 😂

**Mais savez-vous quoi? J'AI ADORÉ ÇA QUAND MÊME!**

Et c'est probablement une des choses que j'ai le plus appréciées. Même quand on est mauvais, même quand on échoue des missions, l'histoire continue! Le jeu ne nous empêche pas de profiter de son excellent scénario simplement parce qu'on n'est pas particulièrement doué dans sa portion gestion. Mes échecs faisaient partie de mon aventure et j'ai vraiment aimé cette approche.

Bon, j'avoue aussi que j'aurais apprécié un peu plus d'intimité avec Blazer... mais ça, c'est un autre sujet! 😏

Bref, Dispatch est une expérience narrative absolument fantastique. J'ai ri, j'ai été surpris, je me suis attaché aux personnages et, surtout, j'avais constamment envie de continuer.

**Note finale : 9.5/10.**

Un immense bravo à toute l'équipe. Vous avez créé quelque chose de vraiment spécial!
